site_selection_index_test: Toluidine blue was applied to suspicious oral cavity lesions identified on clinical examination; biopsy site was selected based on dye retention (dark staining areas)
technique: After clinical examination and NBI, patients with slight positivity like lightly or darkly stained with Toluidine blue were processed for biopsy; punch biopsy was taken from the site after applying topical anaesthetic agent
positivity_threshold: Lesions that showed dark blue staining were considered to be positive for premalignant/malignant tissue, while those with light staining, or totally not coloured, were considered negative
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark blue stain; negative: light stain or no stain
comments_index_test: Toluidine blue was applied prior to biopsy in all 44 patients who also received NBI; results were categorized into dark blue, light blue, and not stained, later dichotomized into positive (dark) vs negative (light/none) for diagnostic accuracy calculations.

site_selection_index_test: Patients underwent zero degree endoscopic examination in White Light, followed by NBI on suspicious oral cavity lesions with suspicion of malignancy
technique: Patients underwent zero degree endoscopic examination in White Light, followed by NBI. NBI uses special filters narrowing white light to 400-430 nm (blue) and 525-555 nm (green) bands to enhance visualization of mucosal vascular structure; superficial capillaries appear brown while deeper vessels appear cyan, following Kamath et al. classification: normal mucosa shows clear branching vessels, while neoplastic lesions show scattered brown spots (IPCLs) with well demarcated borders and abnormal vasculature with extension, dilatation, weaving and differing shapes.
positivity_threshold: Lesions which showed irregular borders with weaving, irregular and increase vascularity with increased capillary loops (IPCLs-brown dots) were considered as malignant; altered or hyper vascularity and increased capillaries (brown dots) suggestive of malignancy, while uniform or normal vascularity rules out the malignant chances
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: altered/hyper vascularity with increased capillary loops (brown dots)
comments_index_test: Both index tests (NBI and toluidine blue) were performed on the same 44 patients within-subject, and biopsy site selection was based on combined findings from both tests, with single biopsy taken if both showed the same area, otherwise biopsy from 2 different sites; this complicates independent verification of NBI's standalone diagnostic performance since biopsy decisions were influenced by both tests jointly.

site_selection_index_test: The MB dye (1%) was applied directly on the lesion with cotton bud; the lesion was the site examined in oral leukoplakia patients
technique: Patients rinsed mouth with 1% lactic acid and distilled water for 30 seconds to remove food debris; mucosa was dried with gauze; MB dye (1%) was applied directly on the lesion with cotton bud for 30 seconds; patients rinsed with 1% lactic acid for 30 seconds again to wash out excess dye; pattern of dye retention was assessed by intensity of stain retention.
positivity_threshold: Dark royal blue/deep blue stains of MB were considered as positive retention. Wide, shallow, faint, pale royal blue stains or no retention of the stain were considered as negative for MB retention.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark blue stain retention
blinding_index_test_examiner: The interpretation of stains was conducted initially by two examiners (DS, AK) in all the cases. In case of disagreement between the examiners, third examiner (AS) evaluated the lesion.
comments_index_test: MB staining alone arm; diagnostic accuracy calculated separately from double staining arm using same 50 patients (47 with dysplasia, 3 hyperkeratosis without dysplasia) as reference standard groups.

index_test_arm_label: Vital Staining (Methylene Blue and Lugol's Iodine Double Staining)
index_test_reagent_name: 5% methylene blue followed by 3% Lugol's iodine
site_selection_index_test: Applied to the lesion (MB) and to lesional and perilesional sites (LI)
technique: Patients rinsed mouth with 1% lactic acid and distilled water for 30 seconds; mucosa dried with gauze; MB dye (1%) applied directly on lesion with cotton bud for 30 seconds; rinsed with 1% lactic acid for 30 seconds to wash excess dye; then 3% LI applied to lesional and perilesional sites with a cotton bud for 10-20 seconds. Dark royal blue/deep blue MB stains considered positive; pale/no retention considered negative. Areas staining dark brown with LI considered positive (normal); pale yellow/unstained areas considered negative (dysplastic). Biopsy site selected based on retention of MB and absence of staining of LI.
positivity_threshold: Positive for dysplasia (MB retention positive/dark blue AND LI negative/pale yellow or unstained); Negative (LI positive/dark brown staining) considered normal without dysplasia
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: MB retained (dark blue) and LI unstained/pale yellow (negative for LI)
blinding_index_test_examiner: The interpretation of stains was conducted initially by two examiners (DS, AK) in all the cases; in case of disagreement, a third examiner (AS) evaluated the lesion.
comments_index_test: Double staining used MB first, then LI, on all cases (not vice versa); this order was noted as a study limitation. Sensitivity/specificity/PPV/NPV were all 100% because false negatives from MB alone were reclassified as positive when combined with LI (dark brown/positive LI staining identified the 3 non-dysplastic hyperkeratosis cases as negative).

site_selection_index_test: LOA, positively stained mucosa with toluidine blue and clinical judgment were taken into consideration while selecting the site of biopsy.
technique: Conventional oral examination was performed under incandescent light. Room and operatory lights were dimmed. Oral tissue examined under white light of Identafi® to visualize lesion extent, then instrument switched to violet light for examination of loss of autofluorescence (LOA), where suspicious lesion appears dark. All lesions displaying LOA were blanched to evaluate diascopic fluorescence.
positivity_threshold: Lesions that displayed LOA were considered to be positive and lesions that displayed no LOA or gain of autofluorescence were considered to be negative. On blanching, lesions that achieved complete blanching were considered negative and lesions with partial blanching were considered to be positive for LOA.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: loss of autofluorescence (dark appearance) or partial blanching
comments_index_test: Five cases had positive blanch test and were considered negative for LOA; keratin itself is autofluorescent so dysplasia can be present in thickly keratinized lesions even without LOA, which may explain reduced specificity.

site_selection_index_test: LOA, positively stained mucosa with toluidine blue and clinical judgment were taken into consideration while selecting the site of biopsy.
technique: After examination under white light and violet light for LOA, the light was switched to green-amber light which allowed visualization of the difference in vasculature between normal and abnormal tissue; the examiner could directly observe the vasculature or arrangement of blood vessels of the abnormal tissue, and diffuseness of vasculature was noted.
positivity_threshold: Lesions with diffuse vascularity (appeared darker) under green-amber light were considered positive; lesions without visible vasculature or with vasculature similar to surrounding mucosa were considered negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: diffuse vasculature (darker appearance)
comments_index_test: Green-amber light results (n=63 lesions) are reported alongside violet light in Table 3; sensitivity 78.4%, specificity 15.4%, PPV 56.86%, NPV 33.33%, accuracy 52.38%, p=0.389 (not significant).

site_selection_index_test: LOA, positively stained mucosa with toluidine blue and clinical judgment were taken into consideration while selecting the site of biopsy.
technique: Toluidine blue was prepared as described by Mashberg. Patients rinsed mouth with water for 20 s to remove debris. Then 1% acetic acid was applied for 20 s to remove rosy saliva. The area was gently dried with gauze. Then 1% toluidine blue solution was applied to the lesion with cotton swab for 1 min. After that 1% acetic acid was applied for one minute. Finally, patients rinsed with water again.
positivity_threshold: Dark blue stain uptake was considered positive. A light blue staining or absence of staining was taken as a negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark blue stain uptake
comments_index_test: Toluidine blue was applied sequentially after Identafi® screening on the same lesions in the same patients, so results may not be fully independent between arms.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to suspected lesions identified during screening for oral leukoplakia
technique: The following day, the individuals were treated to TBS (1%) applied to the suspected lesions after prior AA and LIS application the previous day; pre and post images were taken to analyse the stains.
positivity_threshold: NR
positivity_threshold_transformed: NR
calibration_of_assessors: The identification of lesion, application, and assessment of the lesion following vital staining were all standardised across all examiners in the study.
blinding_index_test_assessors: Different examiners were involved in the screening and recruiting of patients, as well as the stain application technique, to prevent bias.
comments_index_test: Total patients in Table 2 (TP+FN+FP+TN=34) is less than the reported sample size of 45, suggesting some patients/lesions were excluded from the 2x2 analysis; reason not explained in text.

site_selection_index_test: Applied on clinically suspected oral leukoplakia lesions identified during screening
technique: On the first day, each patient received AA solution and LIS (Lugol's iodine 3% dilution) application to their suspected lesions; pre and post images were taken to analyse the stains.
positivity_threshold: NR
positivity_threshold_transformed: NR
calibration_of_assessors: The identification of lesion, application, and assessment of the lesion following vital staining were all standardised across all examiners in the study.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Different examiners were involved in the screening and recruiting of patients, as well as the stain application technique, to prevent bias.
comments_index_test: Denominator discrepancy: total n=45 patients received staining, but Table 2 results for Lugol's Iodine (20+3+9+2=34) suggest some patients (likely the epithelial hyperplasia control group of 31.1% ~14 patients) may only be partially reflected or some overlap in categorization; exact per-arm N not separately reported outside the 2x2 table.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to suspected lesions of oral leukoplakia identified during clinical examination
technique: AA solution was applied to the suspected oral leukoplakia lesions on the first day of testing; pre and post images were taken to analyse the stain.
positivity_threshold: Acetowhite appearance indicating dysplasia, associated with reversible coagulation of protein content in the epithelium
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: acetowhite change
calibration_of_assessors: The identification of lesion, application, and assessment of the lesion following vital staining were all standardised across all examiners in the study.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Different examiners were involved in the screening and recruiting of patients, as well as the stain application technique, to prevent bias, though explicit blinding to clinical information is not stated.
comments_index_test: The number analyzed for AA (n=34 from Table 2: 13+10+7+4) differs from the total enrolled sample of 45, suggesting some patients were excluded from the AA sensitivity/specificity analysis; reason not explicitly stated.

index_test_reagent_name: Liquid-based cytology (Orcellex brush sampling, methanol-based ThinPrep PreservCyt fixation, Papanicolaou stain)
index_test_commercial_name: Orcellex brush (Rovers Medical Devices); ThinPrep 2000 Processor and ThinPrep PreservCyt/staining reagents (Hologic Inc)
site_selection_index_test: NR
specimen_collection: OLBC using Orcellex brush was performed on each patient under local anesthesia before undergoing surgical biopsy; brush heads were preserved immediately into vials of methanol-based buffered preservative (ThinPrep PreservCyt) and transferred to a laboratory for processing.
technique: A liquid-based cytology (LBC) slide was automatically prepared for each OLBC sample using the standard protocol of the ThinPrep 2000 processor; LBC slides were Papanicolaou stained by applying ThinPrep staining reagents according to the manufacturer's protocol for cytological assessment. Slides were then blindly and independently assessed by three assessors using the modified 2014 Bethesda system, categorizing into five diagnostic groups.
positivity_threshold: NR
positivity_threshold_transformed: NR
blinding_index_test_assessors: All Papanicolaou-stained LBC slides were blindly and independently assessed by three assessors (M.I., O.K., P.S.) using the modified 2014 Bethesda system.
comments_index_test: This is a single-arm cytology study (multi-class classification into 5 diagnostic categories) rather than a binary positive/negative test; sensitivity/specificity metrics were computed for several category-vs-others comparisons (Table 2), so no single overall positivity threshold applies to the whole arm.

index_test_arm_label: Multispectral Autofluorescence Imaging Endoscopy (L1-SVM, top four features)
site_selection_index_test: Endoscopic multispectral autofluorescence images were acquired from both the suspicious oral lesion identified on clinical examination and a clinically healthy-appearing area on the corresponding contralateral anatomical side.
technique: A 355 nm pulsed laser (1 ns pulse width, ~1 μJ/pulse at the tissue) was used to excite the oral mucosa, and tissue autofluorescence emission was collected at 390±20 nm, 452±22.5 nm, and >500 nm spectral bands, corresponding to collagen, NADH, and FAD, with a 10 mm circular field-of-view, ~100 μm lateral resolution, and <3 s acquisition time per multispectral image; images were then pre-processed (background subtraction, saturation masking, spatial averaging filter, SNR masking, teeth masking) and used to compute absolute and relative multispectral autofluorescence intensity feature maps, which were used to train and cross-validate an L1-regularized SVM classifier via leave-one-patient-out cross-validation, retrained using the top four ranked features.
positivity_threshold: An image-level score threshold was optimized by selecting the point on the ROC curve (from the training set) with maximum sensitivity within the 1-specificity range of 0% to 30%; the validation sample was classified as cancer/precancer if its predicted image-level score was greater than or equal to this optimized threshold, or as benign otherwise.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: image-level SVM posterior probability score ≥ optimized ROC-derived threshold (classified as cancer/precancer)
blinding_index_test_assessors: The tissue biopsy (reference standard) was blinded to the autofluorescence endoscopy imaging acquisition and processing; additionally, during cross-validation each validation image was blinded to the model training.
comments_index_test: This arm represents the best-performing automated L1-SVM classification model using the top four absolute multispectral autofluorescence spectral features (from a pool of 9 absolute features), which achieved 85% sensitivity and 71% specificity; this is distinct from the single-feature L1-SVM model designed to simulate the VELscope device.

site_selection_index_test: Clinical examination of the patient's oral cavity was performed by an experienced head and neck surgeon, followed by acquisition of endoscopic multispectral autofluorescence images from both the suspicious oral lesion and a clinically healthy-appearing area in the corresponding contralateral anatomical side.
technique: A linear L1-SVM model (C=1) using a single spectral feature consisting of the combined normalized autofluorescence intensities at the 452±22.5 nm and >500 nm emission bands (I452,n + I500,n), simulating the VELscope autofluorescence emission, was trained and cross-validated using LOPOCV; classification performance was compared against the multispectral model.
positivity_threshold: The validation sample was classified as cancer/precancer if its predicted image-level score was greater than or equal to an optimized threshold (selected from ROC analysis on the training set at maximum sensitivity within 1-specificity 0%-30%), or as benign otherwise.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: image-level score ≥ optimized ROC-derived threshold
blinding_index_test_assessors: The validation sample used for classification was blinded to the model training, and the biopsy was blinded to the autofluorescence imaging acquisition and processing.
comments_index_test: This arm is a computational simulation of the VELscope device using a single combined spectral feature (I452,n+I500,n) derived from the same multispectral autofluorescence images used in the main model, not an actual VELscope device measurement; authors note further validation with the actual VELscope system is needed.

site_selection_index_test: NR
specimen_collection: Oral brush biopsy using Orcellex® brush (Rovers Medical Devices, the Netherlands) under local anaesthesia before surgical biopsies
technique: Oral brush samples were preserved in methanol-based preservative vials (ThinPrep® PreservCyt) and processed into liquid-based cytology slides using the ThinPrep® 2000 processor; cytological assessment of Papanicolaou-stained ThinPrep slides was carried out using the modified 2014 Bethesda Cervical Cytology grading system, classifying cases as atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance, low-grade SIL, high-grade SIL or OSCC.
positivity_threshold: NR
positivity_threshold_transformed: NR
comments_index_test: OLBC grading was based on the modified Bethesda system with four categories (undetermined significance SIL, low-grade SIL, high-grade SIL, OSCC); one case was excluded due to staining defect, leaving 71 analyzed for cytological accuracy.

index_test_reagent_name: MSH-6, MSH-2, MLH-1, PMS-2 antibodies (Agilent Dako)
site_selection_index_test: Brush biopsy performed on clinically diagnosed oral leukoplakia or OSCC lesions
specimen_collection: Oral brush biopsy samples using Orcellex brush, preserved in methanol-based preservative, from which cell blocks were prepared via thromboplastin-plasma method
technique: Standard ICC staining was performed on 4-μm sections of cell blocks for MSH-6, MSH-2, MLH-1, and PMS-2. Antibody expression was scored based on staining intensity (0-3) and percentage of positive cells (1-4), multiplied to give an index score per protein per slide; the cumulative index score for each case was the sum of the index scores of the four proteins, assessed blindly by two independent observers counting >500 cells at ×100 magnification in 10 random fields.
positivity_threshold: Cumulative index score cut-offs: 7.76-12 = No dysplasia; 5.51-7.75 = Low-risk lesion; 2.76-5.5 = High-risk lesion; 0-2.75 = OSCC
positivity_threshold_transformed: Lower cumulative MMR index score indicates higher disease severity (OSCC); higher score indicates no dysplasia
calibration_of_assessors: For antibody optimization, three cell lines prepared as cell blocks were used: PE/CA-PJ15 (OSCC), DOK (dysplastic oral keratinocytes) and HOK (normal oral keratinocytes)
blinding_index_test_assessors: Each slide was assessed blindly by two independent observers
comments_index_test: The cumulative index is a composite score derived from ICC expression of four MMR proteins (MSH-6, MSH-2, MLH-1, PMS-2) on cell blocks; this is distinct from the OLBC cytology grading and the combined index (which merges cumulative index with OLBC scores). Accuracy for this arm was lower (75.81%) compared to OLBC grading alone (95.07%) and combined index (92.25%).

index_test_arm_label: Combined index (OLBC grading + Cumulative MMR index)
index_test_reagent_name: Papanicolaou stain + MSH-6, MSH-2, MLH-1, PMS-2 antibodies
site_selection_index_test: Lesions clinically diagnosed as OLK or OSCC; oral brush biopsy performed on these lesions before surgical biopsy
specimen_collection: Oral brush biopsy using Orcellex® brush obtained before surgical biopsy, preserved in ThinPrep PreservCyt vials, and cell blocks prepared from remaining cells using the thromboplastin-plasma method
technique: Combined index = sum of OLBC cytology grading score (Bethesda system) and cumulative MMR index score (sum of index scores for MSH-6, MSH-2, MLH-1, PMS-2, each calculated as staining intensity score x percentage-positive-cells score); cut-offs determined via ROC curve coordinates and Youden's index
positivity_threshold: Combined index score cut-offs: 8.26-12 = No dysplasia; 5.76-8.25 = Low-grade lesion; 3.76-5.75 = High-grade lesion; 0-3.75 = OSCC
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: combined index score below threshold per category (higher score = less severe, lower score = more severe/OSCC)
calibration_of_assessors: Each ICC slide was assessed blindly by two independent observers counting more than 500 cells at ×100 magnification in 10 random fields; antibody optimization was performed using three cell lines (PE/CA-PJ15, DOK, HOK)
blinding_index_test_assessors: ICC slides were assessed blindly by two independent observers, but blinding specifically to histopathological reference standard result is not explicitly stated
comments_index_test: The combined index integrates both OLBC cytology grading and cumulative MMR immunocytochemistry index scores; accuracy of combined index (92.25%) was higher than cumulative index alone (75.81%) but lower than OLBC grading alone (95.07%)

site_selection_index_test: All cases presenting clinically suspected potentially malignant and malignant oral cavity lesions were included; those with inaccessible lesion sites for sampling were excluded
specimen_collection: Material obtained from the oral lesion using a commercially available medium-bristle toothbrush, deposited onto a glass slide
technique: Patients rinsed the oral cavity with normal saline before the procedure; a commercially available medium-bristle toothbrush was used to obtain material from the lesion with minimal discomfort, and the material was deposited onto a glass slide to prepare smears (H and E, PAP, and MGG stained).
positivity_threshold: Lesions were categorized into four diagnostic categories per the oral Bethesda system: NILM, LSIL, HSIL, and SCC; malignancy detection statistics classified LSIL/HSIL/SCC as positive for malignancy versus NILM as negative
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: LSIL/HSIL/SCC (abnormal cytology); negative: NILM
comments_index_test: The BR technique smears were also cytocentrifuged to create the separate BRCC arm; results for BR and BRCC were often identical in diagnostic accuracy tables, suggesting overlapping analysis population but distinct processing methods.

index_test_reagent_name: Normal saline (15 mL) processing fluid with toothbrush-derived material
site_selection_index_test: Patients presenting with clinically suspected potentially malignant and malignant oral cavity lesions were referred to the Department of Pathology for cytopathological evaluation
specimen_collection: Material obtained from the brush cytology technique (using a medium-bristle toothbrush) was subsequently immersed in normal saline (15 mL), mixed well, and subjected to cytocentrifugation to prepare the BRCC smears
technique: The material obtained from the toothbrush (BR technique) was immersed in 15 mL normal saline, mixed well, and subjected to cytocentrifugation using program No. 1 (1250 rpm for 3 min) to prepare the BRCC smears; for each case, one H and E-stained, one PAP-stained, and one MGG-stained smear were prepared, with H and E/PAP smears fixed in isopropyl alcohol and MGG smears air-dried.
positivity_threshold: NR
positivity_threshold_transformed: NR
comments_index_test: BRCC and BR technique diagnostic results were reported together in Tables 2-3 and text (e.g., 'BR technique and BRCC technique showed 21 true-positive cases...'), so some diagnostic statistics (sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV) are combined for BR and BRCC rather than reported separately for BRCC alone.

site_selection_index_test: Clinically suspected potentially malignant and malignant oral cavity lesions were referred to the Department of Pathology for cytopathological evaluation
specimen_collection: Material was scraped from the oral cavity lesion using a commercially available plastic ice cream spoon and deposited onto a glass slide
technique: Patients rinsed the oral cavity with normal saline before the procedure. Modified scrape cytology was performed using a commercially available plastic ice cream spoon to obtain material with minimal discomfort. The material obtained was deposited onto a glass slide. For each technique, one H and E-stained smear, one PAP-stained smear, and one MGG-stained smear were prepared. Smears for H and E and PAP were fixed using isopropyl alcohol; smears for MGG were air-dried.
positivity_threshold: Lesions categorized according to the oral Bethesda system into NILM, LSIL, HSIL, and SCC; positive for malignancy was defined based on cytological diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) as determined by statistical values for detection of malignancy using the Galen and Gambino method
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: SCC on cytology
comments_index_test: In the SR technique, definitive diagnosis could not be offered in two cases (7.41%), reducing the analyzed sample to 25 (Table 1) and diagnosis was offered in only 21 of 23 histopathologically confirmed cases (91.3%). Fungal infection was noted as an additional finding.

index_test_reagent_name: Normal saline (15 mL) processing fluid with scrape-derived material
site_selection_index_test: Patients presenting with clinically suspected potentially malignant and malignant oral cavity lesions were referred to the Department of Pathology for cytopathological evaluation
specimen_collection: Material was obtained by scraping the lesion with a commercially available plastic ice cream spoon (modified scrape cytology technique), then immersed in 15 mL normal saline and subjected to cytocentrifugation to prepare the SRCC smear.
technique: Material obtained from the SR technique (using a plastic ice cream spoon) was immersed in 15 mL normal saline solution, mixed well, and subjected to cytocentrifugation using program No. 1 (1250 rpm for 3 min). One H and E-stained smear, one PAP-stained smear, and one MGG-stained smear were prepared for each case.
positivity_threshold: A case was considered cytologically positive for malignancy if it was diagnosed as squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) on cytology, categorized per the oral Bethesda system (NILM, LSIL, HSIL, SCC); true-positive/negative/false-positive/false-negative determined by concordance with histopathological diagnosis of malignant vs. benign lesions.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: cytological diagnosis of malignancy (SCC)
comments_index_test: The SRCC technique used material obtained from the modified scrape cytology (SR) procedure, which was then cytocentrifuged with normal saline; diagnostic accuracy statistics (sensitivity, specificity) for SRCC appear to be based on the same 21 total malignant/benign cases as reported for SR technique detection of malignancy in the 'Statistical values for detection of malignancy' section, though the text labels this as 'SRCC technique showed 20 true-positive cases...' with a total of 22, creating a minor discrepancy between the diagnosis-offered n=22 and the true/false positive counts summing to 22 (20+1+0+1).

site_selection_index_test: COE encompasses a manual and visual examination of intra- and extra-oral sites; lesions were then classified into benign or malignant.
technique: Patients underwent a complete clinical interview followed by conventional oral examination (COE), a manual and visual examination of intra- and extra-oral sites; based on clinical characteristics, examiners classified lesions into benign or malignant.
positivity_threshold: Classified as suspected malignant lesion based on clinical characteristics
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: clinically suspected malignant lesion
calibration_of_assessors: One examiner (s-GD) underwent a 1-year post-graduate training program in oral medicine prior to the study.
blinding_index_test_assessors: Vel-E was performed on the basis of clinical information and in the absence of histological data; biopsy/histology was performed after COE and Vel-E, implying COE was done without knowledge of reference standard result.
comments_index_test: COE was performed by two examiners (u-GD and s-GD) with differing training; results reported separately for each in Table 2.

site_selection_index_test: Vel-E performed on lesions identified during clinical oral examination (COE) based on clinical characteristics, in the absence of histological data.
technique: The device was used, maintaining a distance of approximately 5 cm from the oral cavity to optimize the visualization of the natural tissue fluorescence and, if necessary, darken the operating theatre to reduce natural light and bring it to an acceptable level.
positivity_threshold: In the presence of LAF (loss of autofluorescence, i.e., darker appearance compared to surrounding areas), the Vel-E is defined positive.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: loss of autofluorescence (LAF)
calibration_of_assessors: One general dentist underwent a 1-year post-graduate training program in oral medicine at the Oral Medicine Unit, Federico II University of Naples, Italy, prior to performing Vel-E.
blinding_index_test_assessors: The Vel-E examiners performed the test on the basis of clinical information and in the absence of histological data, indicating they were blinded to the reference standard result at the time of index testing.
comments_index_test: Two examiners (u-GD and s-GD) each independently performed Vel-E on all 35 patients; results are reported separately for each examiner in Table 2.

index_test_commercial_name: GEMINI Medical Diagnostic System's DNA Image Cytometer
site_selection_index_test: Brush samples were collected from the same oral mucosal lesion sites as the incisional biopsies
specimen_collection: Patient rinses mouth with water, then clinician gently scrapes oral mucosal lesions at least 10 times using a flexible cotton cytology brush; brush head stored in tube with cell preservation solution and sent to lab within 24 hours
technique: Samples were examined using a liquid-based thin-layer cell preparation and Feulgen staining. The samples were deposited on microscope slides and stained with the Feulgen-thionin technique, which stains the nuclei dark blue without staining the cytoplasm, and subsequently scanned with the GEMINI Medical Diagnostic System's DNA Image Cytometer (DNA-ICM). DNA quantitative analysis was performed only when specimens contained at least 300 epithelial cell nuclei that were normalized to normal epithelial cell nuclei.
positivity_threshold: The oral specimen was classified as having abnormal DNA content if the aneuploid group has more than 3 nuclei (1% of at least 300 nuclei), or the hyperdiploid group had 5% of the total number of nuclei, or the tetraploid group had 10% of the total number of nuclei
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: abnormal DNA content (aneuploid >3 nuclei/1%, hyperdiploid ≥5%, or tetraploid ≥10% of nuclei)
blinding_index_test_assessors: DNA image cytometry was performed blinded to the histological results
comments_index_test: The DNA-ICM technique used cotton brushes which the authors note may reduce accuracy due to inability to obtain cells from the entire epithelial layer of the oral mucosa. This is the only index test arm in this single-test study.

index_test_reagent_name: DNA index (DI) ≥ 3.5 (DNA content ≥ 7.0c) via DNA-image cytometry on cytobrush sample
site_selection_index_test: Brushing was performed at the same location as the lesion, covering the whole lesion, before scalpel biopsy was taken from the same site.
specimen_collection: The brush sample was collected by performing brushing of the whole lesion with a liquid-based brush kit (MotiSavant, Motic, Xiamen, China).
technique: Cytobrush samples were processed by DNA image cytometry (DNA-ICM) per the manufacturer's protocol (MotiSavant), analyzing nuclear DNA content to determine the DNA index (DI); at least 1 aneuploid cell with DI ≥ 3.5 (DNA content ≥ 7.0c) was used as the optimal cut-off, determined via ROC/Youden index analysis, and analyses were performed by individuals blinded to histopathological results.
positivity_threshold: At least 1 aneuploid cell with a DNA index (DI) ≥ 3.5 (DNA content ≥ 7.0c)
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: DI ≥ 3.5 (aneuploid)
blinding_index_test_assessors: DNA-ICM analyses were conducted by individuals (C.L. and Y.Z.) who were blinded to the histopathological results, because the DNA content analyses were completed before the histopathological diagnoses.
comments_index_test: This arm reflects the standalone DNA aneuploidy test (DI ≥ 3.5) results, separate from the combined risk model arm (which adds lesion site and lesion type); diagnostic accuracy figures in Tables 2 and 3 correspond to this arm's training and test set performance.

index_test_arm_label: Risk Model (DNA Aneuploidy + Lateral/Ventral Tongue + Non-homogenous Type, Score ≥ 4)
index_test_reagent_name: Composite risk score derived from DNA aneuploidy (DI ≥ 3.5), lateral/ventral tongue site, and non-homogenous lesion type
site_selection_index_test: Cytobrush biopsy performed at the same location as the lesion prior to scalpel biopsy; lesion site (lateral/ventral tongue vs. others) and lesion type (homogenous vs. non-homogenous) also assessed clinically at the same lesion.
specimen_collection: The brush sample was collected by performing brushing of the whole lesion with a liquid-based brush kit (MotiSavant, Motic, Xiamen, China).
technique: A risk model was constructed using multivariate logistic regression combining three independent significant variables: lateral/ventral tongue lesion site, non-homogenous lesion type, and DNA aneuploidy (DI ≥ 3.5) determined by DNA-ICM on cytobrush samples. Each patient's total risk score was the sum of the β-coefficient-derived risk scores for these three variables (risk scores: lateral/ventral tongue = 1.97, non-homogenous type = 2.03, DI ≥ 3.5 = 2.57), ranging from 0–6.57. An ROC curve with maximum Youden index analysis was used to determine the optimal cut-off of the total risk score.
positivity_threshold: Risk score ≥ 4
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: risk score ≥ 4
calibration_of_assessors: DNA-ICM analyses were conducted by individuals (C.L. and Y.Z.) who were blinded to the histopathological results; no specific calibration/training procedure described for risk model application.
blinding_index_test_assessors: DNA-ICM analyses were conducted by individuals blinded to the histopathological results because DNA content analyses were completed before histopathological diagnoses.
comments_index_test: This arm represents a composite/combined risk model score (not a single laboratory test) integrating DNA aneuploidy status with two clinical features (lesion site and lesion type); values extracted here reflect the training set (n=608) results reported in Table 2; the same model was independently validated in the test set (n=202, Table 3) with different performance metrics.

positivity_threshold: NR
positivity_threshold_transformed: NR

site_selection_index_test: Thorough intraoral clinical examination for the location of the most representative mucosal site for the white and red lesions
technique: Patients rinsed mouth with distilled water for one minute, then 1% RB solution (1 gm RB powder in 100 mL distilled water) was applied for two minutes over the clinically assessed site, followed by a one-minute distilled water rinse to remove excess dye; the stained lesional area was then examined intraorally and staining intensity evaluated visually as mild, moderate, intense, or negative.

technique: Microbiopsy performed using a dermatological ring curette with a 3 mm diameter at the intensely stained region, scraping the lesional area gently with the sharp edge of the curette to obtain pinpoint mucosal bleeding ensuring the basal layer was sampled. Multiple tissue fragments obtained were routinely processed, embedded, and sectioned for H&E staining, coded randomly, and observed under a light microscope; epithelial dysplasia was graded using criteria given by Banoczy J and Csiba A.
positivity_threshold: Histopathological indicators of epithelial dysplasia (cellular and architectural changes) present, graded using criteria given by Banoczy J and Csiba A (mild, moderate, severe dysplasia considered positive)
