Paper: Martín-Muñoz-2025-Predictive value of a non-in (DTA- updated December 2025)
site_selection_index_test: A visual examination of each lesion was conducted first, and then GOCCLES® scanning was performed on the same clinically identified lesion to detect areas of fluorescence loss; the most suitable biopsy area was determined afterward based on investigator judgment, informed by both oral examination and GOCCLES®/TB findings.
technique: Scanning was performed using the GOCCLES® device (Pierrel S.p.A-Italy) to detect areas of fluorescence loss indicative of possible dysplasia. The tissue was irradiated with a UV light source from an SDi Radii Xpert polymerizing lamp (SDI, Australia) with a wavelength of 440–480 nm and an intensity of 1500 mW/cm2 applied at a distance of 20 cm from the lesion. The irradiated tissue was observed through the GOCCLES® device and photographs were taken using the mobile camera filter included in the device kit with a Xiaomi Redmi Note 9S smartphone.
positivity_threshold: Lesions showing fluorescence loss, visible as brown or dark green areas through the device, were classified as GOCCLES® positive. Lesions without visible dark areas, where all tissue appeared within the green spectrum, were classified as GOCCLES® negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: fluorescence loss (dark/brown or dark green areas)
calibration_of_assessors: All biopsy procedures and the processes described above were performed by the same professional with specialized training in oral medicine.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded — the same professional performed all procedures including biopsy site selection, introducing a risk of incorporation bias.
comments_index_test: The examiner who applied and interpreted GOCCLES® also performed the oral examination, TB staining, and selected the biopsy site, raising risk of incorporation bias as noted by the authors as a study limitation.

Paper: Martín-Muñoz-2025-Predictive value of a non-in (DTA- updated December 2025)
site_selection_index_test: TB was applied to the entire visually identified lesion (same lesion examined visually, photographed, and scanned with GOCCLES®) rather than to a specific pre-selected sub-site.
technique: TB staining was performed following the technique described by Mashberg (1983). Lesions with intense blue staining were classified as positive for TB, while those with no staining or with only slight or diffuse staining were considered negative. Photographs were captured using the previously mentioned camera.
positivity_threshold: Lesions with intense blue staining were classified as positive for TB, while those with no staining or with only slight or diffuse staining were considered negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: intense/dark blue staining
calibration_of_assessors: All biopsy procedures and the processes described above (including TB staining) were performed by the same professional with specialized training in oral medicine.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded; the same professional performed the oral examination, GOCCLES® scanning, TB staining, biopsy site selection, and biopsy.
comments_index_test: TB staining was performed after GOCCLES® scanning on the same lesion in the same patient visit, using the technique described by Mashberg (1983); guidelines by Mashberg (1980) were also referenced for interpretation.

Paper: Martín-Muñoz-2025-Predictive value of a non-in (DTA- updated December 2025)
site_selection_index_test: Same site selection as the individual GOCCLES® and TB examinations; both tests were applied to the same lesion, with the most suitable biopsy area later determined by the investigator
technique: The combined method used the concordant results (both positive or both negative) of the GOCCLES® scan and toluidine blue staining performed sequentially on the same lesion; no separate combined technique was applied beyond comparing the two individual test results.
positivity_threshold: A case was classified as positive for the combined method only if both GOCCLES® and toluidine blue results were concordant and positive; concordant negative results were classified as negative
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: concordant positive on both GOCCLES® and toluidine blue
blinding_index_test_assessors: Not blinded; the same professional who performed the biopsy also selected the biopsy site, introducing a risk of incorporation bias
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded; the same examiner performed all procedures (GOCCLES®, TB staining, and biopsy site selection) for each patient
comments_index_test: The combined arm is not an independent index test but a post-hoc concordance analysis restricted to the 18/32 cases where GOCCLES® and TB gave concordant results; this selective subset (excluding discordant cases) may bias diagnostic accuracy estimates for the combined method.

site_selection_index_test: The samples from the oral cavity lesion or suspicious area were collected by a cytology brush.
specimen_collection: Samples were collected from the oral cavity lesion or suspicious area using a cytology brush and transferred onto a glass slide.
technique: The conventional alcohol-fixed smears were stained according to the Papanicolaou method and interpreted by the cytopathologist. Specimens were diagnosed according to categories: negative (normal squamous cells/reactive or inflammatory changes), atypical (atypical cells present, e.g., superficial cell dyskeratosis), suspicious (dyskeratotic cells of parabasal type or few malignant cells present), positive (malignant cells present), and not sufficient (few or poorly preserved squamous cells or obscuring bacterial colonization).
positivity_threshold: "positive" indicated malignant cells present
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: malignant cells present
calibration_of_assessors: Smears were interpreted by the cytopathologist; no specific calibration/training process was reported.
comments_index_test: PAP staining results served as one of three index tests compared to histopathology; exact n received/analyzed per arm not separately stated beyond the 60 total patients and Table 3 breakdown by SCC (30) and benign (30).

site_selection_index_test: The samples from the oral cavity lesion or suspicious area were collected by a cytology brush.
specimen_collection: Samples were collected from the oral cavity lesion or suspicious area using a cytology brush, transferred onto a glass slide, and the conventional alcohol-fixed smears were prepared.
technique: Glass slides with harvested material were fixed in 97% alcohol; TP4303 solution (0.5 µg) was added to cover the cell area, kept in dark at 22°C for ~20 minutes, then rinsed with deionized water and air dried. 20 µl of DAPI was added, a coverslip placed, and the slide observed using a fluorescent microscope. Cells with TP4303 interaction showed dark orange fluorescence around the nucleus (VPAC receptor positive); absence of VPAC receptors showed only DAPI-bound nucleus in dark blue.
positivity_threshold: Cells with TP4303 interaction presented with dark orange fluorescence around the nucleus indicating presence of VPAC receptor molecules; reports were read as positive for VPAC receptors (malignant cells) or negative for VPAC receptors (non-malignant cells).
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark orange fluorescence around nucleus (VPAC receptor expression)
comments_index_test: NR

site_selection_index_test: NR
specimen_collection: Patients were asked to gargle with 20 cc of normal saline for a few minutes and were asked to spit out the contents into a collecting cup. The collected fluid was centrifuged and the sediment was transferred onto a glass slide and fixed in 97% alcohol.
technique: The collected fluid was centrifuged and the sediment was transferred onto a glass slide and fixed in 97% alcohol. The rest of the procedure was as mentioned above (TP4303 solution (0.5 µg) added, kept in dark at 22°C for approximately 20 minutes, rinsed with deionized water, air dried, then 20 µl DAPI added, coverslip placed, and slide observed using fluorescent microscope).
positivity_threshold: Cells with TP4303 interaction presented themselves with dark orange fluorescence around the nucleus and thereby indicated the presence of VPAC receptor molecules around the cell surface. In the absence of VPAC receptors, only the DAPI-bound cell nucleus was seen in dark blue.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: orange fluorescence around nucleus (VPAC receptor binding)
comments_index_test: Oral gargle VPAC staining uses the same TP4303/DAPI fluorescent staining protocol as brush cytology VPAC staining, differing only in specimen collection method (gargle sediment vs. brush cytology).

site_selection_index_test: The irradiating light was set perpendicular to the lesion and the irradiation range was set to about 10 cm; ROIs for the lesion and control area were established in FV images, with the control ROI set at a distance away in the same sub-site of the oral cavity in normal mucosa in front of the lesion without FVL and oral mucosal lesions
technique: FV images were taken in a room that was as dark as possible using OIs (ORALOOK® or IllumiScan®, used randomly, left to the attending physician). The irradiating light was set perpendicular to the lesion and the irradiation range was set to about 10 cm. In subjective evaluations, oral conditions and FV images were compared to evaluate FVR, FVA or FVL in lesions. Image processing analysis was performed on the FV images using Image J software; ROIs for lesion and control area were established, and the state of the lesion ROI was expressed as a surface plot with color mapping.
positivity_threshold: In subjective evaluation, we defined a positive case as FVL and a negative case as only FVA or FVR by two or more screenings using the surface plot as a reference
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: FVL (fluorescence visualization loss); negative: FVA or FVR
comments_index_test: Subjective evaluation was determined by two or more screenings ('by two or more screenings using the surface plot as a reference'), suggesting multiple assessors were involved, but the number, qualifications, and blinding status of these assessors relative to the reference standard (biopsy) are not explicitly reported, which is a potential risk-of-bias concern.

site_selection_index_test: Patients presenting with non-healing ulcers or patches persisting for more than two weeks, or unresponsive to treatment, underwent detailed history and clinical examination to identify suspected oral lesions for staining
technique: Methylene blue was applied as a dye rinse (solution A: 1% malachite, dimethyl-sulfoxide, glycerol, and 1% methylene blue solution). Participants first rinsed with solution B (purified water, raspberry flavor, 1% lactic acid) for 20 seconds to clear hypersalivation/debris, then the mucosa was dried with a triple syringe and gauze. Solution A was applied, and after a 20 second wait, patients rinsed again with solution B for 20 seconds to remove excess stain (using cotton rolls to clear the surface if needed). Stain intensity was noted by one observer after the final rinse. Local, stippled, concentrated blue stains indicated a positive reaction, while wide/faint blue stains indicated a negative reaction.
positivity_threshold: The indicators of positive reaction include local, stipules and concentrated blue stains while wide and faint blue stains indicate a negative reaction. If the stain retained, positive result was recorded and vice versa.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: localized concentrated/stippled deep blue stain retained; negative: wide, faint, or no stain
comments_index_test: The stain intensity was assessed by a single observer; no blinding or calibration procedures were reported, which is a potential source of bias. Also, in Table 2, the study collapses the 4-category staining result (deep vs faint) against binary histopathology outcome, and Table 2 totals (66 deep + 11 faint = 77) differ slightly from the narrative TP/FP/FN/TN counts described in the text (60 TP, 6 FP, 4 FN, 7 TN = 77), which are internally consistent but framed differently in Table 2's row structure.

site_selection_index_test: A region of interest (ROI) was defined in the lesion area of the G-image based on intraoral photographs and intraoral findings by the attending physician; NOM ROIs were set at the sublingual mucosa, buccal mucosa, the transition area from the molar attachment gingiva to the buccal mucosa and the mucosa on the floor of the oral cavity
technique: Lesions were photographed under white light with a digital camera and then photographed using IllumiScan® in a dark room, with the lens held approximately 30 mm from the lesion; images were transferred to a computer and analysed using ImageJ, dividing each image into RGB components, creating a black-and-white G-image from the green component, defining a ROI in the lesion area, and expressing fluorescence intensity (FI) at 256 levels (0–255); average FI, standard deviation (SD), and coefficient of variation (CV = SD/average FI × 10) were then calculated.
positivity_threshold: Assuming an average FI cut-off of 98.5, the sensitivity and specificity were 71.2% and 67.8%, respectively; an SD cut-off of 11.2, sensitivity 83.1% and specificity 65.6%; a CV cut-off of 1.70, sensitivity 72.9% and specificity 78.3% (cut-offs defined based on the Youden index post-hoc)
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: CV ≥1.70 (post-hoc ROC-derived cutoff, not pre-specified)
comments_index_test: The positivity thresholds (FI, SD, CV cut-offs) were derived retrospectively via ROC/Youden index analysis rather than pre-specified before testing, which should be considered when assessing risk of bias for index test interpretation.

site_selection_index_test: Next, scrape the entire lesion with the coverslip.
specimen_collection: The lesion was scraped using a coverslip to collect cells, which were then spread onto a glass slide and fixed.
technique: Two glass slides and a coverslip were used per lesion. The patient's name, date, and anatomic location were written on the frosted end of the slide. After removing excess saliva with gauze, the entire lesion was scraped with the coverslip vigorously enough to be noticeable (may cause slight bleeding) but not painful. The harvested cells were spread onto the glass slide from the frosted end to the other end, ensuring visible white, filmy debris. The slide was immediately placed in a Koplin jar with fixative (80% alcohol) to prevent cell degeneration. The procedure was repeated for a second smear on the same lesion, and a different coverslip was used for each lesion if multiple lesions were present.
positivity_threshold: NR
positivity_threshold_transformed: NR
comments_index_test: The study reports overall sensitivity of 83.4% and specificity of 100% for exfoliative cytology compared to biopsy/histopathology, but does not specify exact numbers of patients or lesions tested with cytology versus the total cohort of 73 patients described in Table 1, nor a specific cytological positivity threshold (e.g., dysplasia grade).

site_selection_index_test: NR
specimen_collection: Sediment cytology smears were prepared from the leftover formalin fixative of biopsy specimen bottles: the fixative was centrifuged at 3000 rpm for 5 min, supernatant discarded, sediment washed twice in normal saline, and smeared onto albumen-coated slides.
technique: The fixative fluid from the original specimen bottle was centrifuged at 3000 rpm for 5 min; the supernatant was discarded and the sediments washed twice in normal saline and used for smear preparation on albumen-coated slides. Smears were fixed in 95% ethanol with 3% glacial acetic acid (Biofix spray) and stained with Papanicolaou (PAP) stain.
positivity_threshold: Class I-normal, class II-atypia, class III-intermediate, class IV-suggestive of cancer, class V-positive for cancer; reported as negative (Class I) or positive (Class II and III) for OPMDs and as positive (Class IV and V) for oral malignant lesions.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: Class II-V cytologic atypia/malignant changes (Class II-III for OPMDs, Class IV-V for malignant lesions)
blinding_index_test_examiner: The prepared smears were analysed by two observers to reduce the inter-observer bias.
comments_index_test: Sediment cytology was performed on sediments obtained from the formalin fixative of the biopsy specimen bottle (biopsy sediment cytology), not by direct in-vivo staining or scraping of an oral site; hence site_selection_index_test and specimen_collection reflect biopsy-derived fixative sediment processing rather than in-vivo lesion site selection.

site_selection_index_test: Site selection was based on clinically suspicious oral lesions identified during conventional oral examination (COE); VELscope was applied to these same lesions at the same appointment.
technique: After COE, autofluorescence visualization (AFV) was achieved by a handheld VELscope (C Ultra by Technomax Corporation, Pune, Maharashtra); findings were categorized as AFL (loss of fluorescence) or AFR (retained or no loss of fluorescence).
positivity_threshold: Positive result defined as Loss of Fluorescence (AFL) on VELscope examination; retained fluorescence (AFR) considered negative. Two separate reference comparisons were made: (1) dysplasia/malignancy vs. no dysplasia, and (2) high-risk lesions (moderate/severe dysplasia or carcinoma in situ) vs. low-risk lesions (no/mild dysplasia).
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: autofluorescence loss (AFL)
comments_index_test: The study reports two separate 2x2 analyses using different positivity thresholds for the reference standard (dysplasia/malignancy vs. no dysplasia in Table 1, yielding sensitivity 77.77%/specificity 25%; and high-risk vs. low-risk lesions in Table 2, yielding sensitivity 90.47%/specificity 44.44%), but the index test (VELscope AFL/AFR classification) itself is the same across both comparisons.

site_selection_index_test: All study participants with suspicious OPMDs (as identified during conventional oral examination) underwent a second examination using the fluorescence light-based handheld device
technique: OralID is a battery-operated, handheld oral examination light that emits a visible blue light (435–460 nm) that shines directly into the oral cavity allowing the clinician to view the tissue fluorescence during the oral exam. Oral lesions illuminating bright green or white green were recorded as no OPMDs; those with lack of fluorescence, dark areas, or a combination of bright green/white green and dark areas were recorded as OPMDs.
positivity_threshold: Oral lesions with lack of fluorescence or dark areas, or a combination of bright green/white green fluorescent and dark areas were recorded as OPMDs (positive); lesions illuminating bright green or white green were recorded as no OPMDs (negative)
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: loss of fluorescence/dark areas
blinding_index_test_examiner: The same dentist who performed the conventional oral examination also performed the fluorescent oral evaluation, which could result in a high likelihood of report bias.
comments_index_test: The same highly trained clinician performed both the conventional oral exam (used to select suspicious lesions for fluorescence testing) and the fluorescence exam, which the authors acknowledge as a limitation increasing risk of report bias; also, the clinician's high skill in conventional exam may have limited the added value detected for autofluorescence.

index_test_commercial_name: Velscope (LED Dental, Burnaby, British Columbia, Canada)
site_selection_index_test: All patients clinically diagnosed with OPMDs during a screening camp underwent Velscope examination of their oral lesions; no specific multi-site selection protocol beyond the identified lesion was described.
technique: Patients underwent oral examination using the Velscope device before incisional biopsy. Examinations were conducted in a dark room, with patients wearing special glasses provided in the Velscope kit. A blue light (400–460 nm) was directed onto the oral tissues, and the emitted fluorescence was assessed visually.
positivity_threshold: Lesions exhibiting loss of autofluorescence (FVL) appeared as dark areas, suggesting dysplasia.
positivity_threshold_transformed: Positive: loss of fluorescence visualization (FVL, dark area)
calibration_of_assessors: Initially, 10 patients were examined to calibrate the visualization of colours for consistent assessment across the study.
comments_index_test: The study included only one index test arm (Velscope); calibration of 10 patients prior to the main assessment may reduce measurement variability but blinding of examiners to biopsy results was not explicitly reported, raising potential risk of bias.

site_selection_index_test: Patients were examined via conventional VOE by experienced senior oral maxillofacial surgeons; VOE assessment covered leukoplakia, erythro leukoplakia, erythroplakia, verrucous hyperplasia, and possibly oral cancer as abnormal findings
technique: Patients were examined via conventional VOE by experienced senior oral maxillofacial surgeons (OMS), assessing for leukoplakia, erythro leukoplakia, erythroplakia, verrucous hyperplasia, and possibly oral cancer as abnormal findings.
positivity_threshold: Abnormal VOE findings, including leukoplakia, erythro leukoplakia, erythroplakia, verrucous hyperplasia, and possible oral cancer
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: any abnormal VOE finding (leukoplakia, erythro leukoplakia, erythroplakia, verrucous hyperplasia, or possible oral cancer)
comments_index_test: No significant difference in VOE judgment was observed among the participating OMS from the three study sites, suggesting reasonable inter-examiner consistency, though formal calibration/training procedures and blinding to reference standard results were not explicitly described.

site_selection_index_test: Oral exfoliated cell specimen was collected by oral swab from the mucosal lesion identified during VOE
specimen_collection: Oral epithelial cells were collected using a foam brush/oral swab from the mucosal lesion and preserved in the 'Epigene' Specimen Collection and Transfer Tube
technique: Genomic DNA was extracted from oral exfoliated cells using the 'Epigene' Nucleic Acid Extraction kit, quantified by NanoDrop spectrophotometer, subjected to bisulfite conversion using the 'Epigene' Bisulfite Conversion Kit (converting unmethylated cytosine to uracil while methylated cytosine remains unchanged), and then ZNF582 methylation levels were determined using the 'Epigene' ZNF582 DNA Detection Kit via quantitative methylation-specific PCR with TaqMan-based technology on a Light Cycler LC480, using COL2A as internal reference; two crossing point (Cp) values were determined and DNA methylation was qualitatively determined per manufacturer's instructions.
positivity_threshold: Two crossing point (Cp) values were determined, one from ZNF582 and the other from COL2A, and DNA methylation was qualitatively determined in accordance with manufacturer's instructions
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: ZNF582 methylation detected (per manufacturer's qualitative cutoff using Cp values)
comments_index_test: The ZNF582m test is a laboratory-based DNA methylation assay performed on oral exfoliated cells collected by swab, distinct from the in-vivo VOE arm; results are qualitative (positive/negative) per manufacturer kit instructions.

site_selection_index_test: All patients were examined by oral medicine specialist for existence of oral lesions following WHO (1987) sequence examination procedure; VELscope was then applied to the identified suspicious lesional and perilesional tissue.
technique: Direct visual examination is then performed by VELscope. Lesional and perilesional tissue was assessed for visual fluorescence retention (VFR) and visual fluorescence loss (VFL) when viewed through the velscopeVX handpiece.
positivity_threshold: Visual fluorescence loss (VFL) when viewed through the VELscope handpiece was considered the abnormal finding, as opposed to visual fluorescence retention (VFR).
positivity_threshold_transformed: Positive: fluorescence visualization loss (FVL)
blinding_index_test_assessors: The histopathology examiner was blinded to the VELscope (DVFE) findings; blinding of the VELscope examiner to histopathology results is not explicitly stated.
comments_index_test: Attempts were made to have the biopsy site cover both COE- and VELscope-positive regions, which could introduce verification/incorporation bias since biopsy site selection may have been influenced by VELscope findings.

site_selection_index_test: Each follow-up visit involved assessment under white light to identify new clinical lesions or alterations to previously identified lesions, with particular attention to sites of previous lesions (e.g., prior oral SCC); after turning off the room light, the oral cavity was viewed with direct FV.
technique: The oral cavity was examined under white light to identify lesions, then room light was turned off and the oral cavity was viewed with the direct FV handheld device, which projects blue excitation light (400-460 nm) coaxially and allows direct visual observation of green-red tissue fluorescence; normal mucosa appears pale green (FV retention), while areas with a distinct reduction to dark green/black are classified as FV loss (FVL), assessed by comparison with adjacent tissue and the contralateral side.
positivity_threshold: Tissue that showed a distinct reduction in the normal pale green and appeared as dark green to black was classified as FV loss (FVL); clinical lesions that retained the normal green autofluorescence were classified as FV retention (FVR). Positive test result corresponds to FVL.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: fluorescence visualization loss (FVL)
blinding_index_test_examiner: The clinicians would then decide whether the oral lesions required biopsy based on standard clinical features (patient history, clinical appearance, and toluidine blue staining results) and not based on the direct FV examination.
comments_index_test: Direct FV results were compared against histology (blinded pathologists CP and LZ) as the reference standard; biopsy decisions were made independently of FV findings, reducing incorporation bias, but explicit statements about blinding of FV assessors to histology results (or vice versa) were not reported.

site_selection_index_test: Scrape smears were done from pathological sites, frequently from mucosal lesions and from other representative sites
specimen_collection: Scrape smears were collected by wooden Ayer's spatula from pathological sites, mainly mucosal lesions and other representative sites
technique: Scrape smears were obtained using a wooden Ayer's spatula from lesion sites; wet smears were fixed in 95% ethanol and stained with Papanicolaou stain, while air-dried smears were stained with Romanowsky (Diff-Quik) stain.
positivity_threshold: NR
positivity_threshold_transformed: NR
comments_index_test: Scrape cytology and FNAC were combined in the 'cytology' diagnostic process in this study; results (Table 3) appear to pool both cytology methods rather than reporting scrape cytology performance separately.

site_selection_index_test: After localizing the lesion, a 23-24G needle attached to a 10 ml disposable plastic syringe was used for FNAC
specimen_collection: Fine-needle aspiration using a 23-24G needle attached to a 10 ml disposable plastic syringe; aspirated material spread on clean numbered slides
technique: After localizing the lesion, a 23-24G needle attached to a 10 ml disposable plastic syringe was used to aspirate material, which was spread on clean numbered slides; wet smears were fixed in 95% ethanol for Papanicolaou stain, and air-dried smears were stained with Romanowsky (Diff-Quik) stain
positivity_threshold: NR
positivity_threshold_transformed: NR
comments_index_test: The study combines FNAC and scrape cytology results together for diagnostic accuracy calculations (Table 3), without separately reporting sensitivity/specificity for FNAC alone; both index tests were performed by the same cytopathologist on all patients.

site_selection_index_test: Participants were screened for oral mucosal lesions, and those lesions were subjected to DrOroscope examination focusing on identifying dysplastic lesions.
technique: On blue light exposure, normal tissues reflect green fluorescence, and there is a loss of fluorescence in abnormal tissues, causing dark areas; images were captured with the image sensor and analyzed using AI-based software algorithms, categorizing lesions into variable, borderline, and severe.
positivity_threshold: Lesions with no dysplastic changes, mild and moderate dysplastic changes, and severe cases were categorized under variable, borderline, and dysplasia, respectively.
positivity_threshold_transformed: Positive: borderline or dysplasia category (loss of fluorescence); Negative: variable category (green fluorescence retained)
calibration_of_assessors: The examiner was trained in the operation of DrOroscope and interpreting its results.
comments_index_test: NR

site_selection_index_test: Lesions clinically diagnosed as oral leukoplakia, oral lichen planus, or oral submucous fibrosis were examined; suspicious areas identified during VELscope examination were subsequently evaluated for biopsy site selection.
technique: Another investigator performed the VELscope examination at a distance of approximately 3–4 inches from the lesion, and noted the nature of tissue fluorescence as either fluorescence retention or fluorescence loss; photographs of fluorescence were recorded for documentation.
positivity_threshold: Normal oral mucosa retains pale green fluorescence (FVR), while areas with dysplasia, inflammation, or increased vascularization lose fluorescence (FVL) and appear dark; fluorescence loss was considered positive.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: fluorescence loss (FVL)
blinding_index_test_examiner: To minimize the risk of bias, the principal investigator conducted the initial clinical evaluation, and another investigator performed the VELscope examination, suggesting separation of roles but no explicit statement of blinding to clinical history.
comments_index_test: Table 3 (OSMF) only reports a positive row for VELscope with no negative row shown, though text states VELscope had 100% sensitivity in OSMF; sample sizes per lesion subgroup (n=10 each) sum to 30 total patients across all three OPMD groups for this index test arm.

site_selection_index_test: Vital staining applied to the suspicious area identified by prior clinical evaluation and VELscope examination
technique: Toluidine blue was applied topically to the suspicious lesion area as part of the vital staining procedure performed after VELscope examination; a dark blue (royal or navy) stain of the entire lesion or a portion of it was considered positive, lack of colour absorption was considered negative, and light or pale blue staining was considered doubtful, with wiping using a cotton swab dipped in 1% acetic acid recommended for doubtful cases to differentiate true retention from surface retention.
positivity_threshold: A dark blue (royal or navy) stain of either the entire lesion or a portion of it was considered positive, a lack of colour absorption by the lesion as negative, and light or pale blue staining as doubtful.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark blue (royal/navy) stain uptake
blinding_index_test_examiner: Another investigator performed an incisional biopsy irrespective of VELscope or staining findings, but blinding of the staining examiner to clinical history/provisional diagnosis is not explicitly reported.
comments_index_test: Toluidine blue was applied as one of three vital stains (with methylene blue and Lugol's iodine) on the same suspicious area in each patient, raising concern about overlapping/sequential application on the same lesion potentially affecting subsequent stain readings.

site_selection_index_test: Vital stains applied on the suspicious area identified by clinical examination and VELscope; lesions positive by both VELscope and vital stains were evaluated for biopsy site selection
technique: After VELscope examination, staining procedures using vital stains (toluidine blue, methylene blue, Lugol's iodine) were performed on the suspicious area; uptake of stain was considered positive for dysplasia, no uptake or light uptake was considered negative, and photographs were documented. Methylene Blue is an acidophilic dye with strong affinity for double-helical DNA; intensity of stain increases with increased chromatin material seen in premalignant/malignant cells; deep blue, local, stippled and patchy stains were considered positive, whereas faint blue, wide, shallow, easily washable stains were considered negative.
positivity_threshold: Deep blue stains, which were local, stippled and patchy were considered to be positive, whereas faint blue stains, which were wide, shallow & could be easily washable, were considered negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: deep/patchy stain uptake; negative: faint/washable stain
blinding_index_test_examiner: To minimize the risk of bias, the principal investigator conducted the initial clinical evaluation, and another investigator performed the VELscope examination, followed by vital staining, while another investigator performed the biopsy irrespective of VELscope or staining findings.
comments_index_test: Denominators for methylene blue specifically (patients/lesions received and analyzed) are not separately reported; overall study N=30 patients across three OPMD groups (10 each) is given, and per-lesion-type contingency tables (Tables 1-3) provide test-specific counts but not aggregated totals for methylene blue across all three lesion types.

site_selection_index_test: Vital stains applied on the suspicious area identified during initial clinical evaluation and VELscope examination; lesions positive by both VELscope and vital stains were evaluated by photographic evidence and biopsy sites were identified.
technique: Vital stains (toluidine blue, methylene blue, Lugol's iodine) were applied on the suspicious area after VELscope examination; uptake of stain was considered positive for dysplasia, no uptake or light uptake was considered negative, and photographs were documented.
positivity_threshold: Since malignant tissues are associated with reduced glycogen content, these remain unstained (negative for glycogen uptake), whereas normal epithelium gets stained brown or black.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: unstained (loss of iodine uptake)
comments_index_test: Lugol's iodine was one of three vital stains (with toluidine blue and methylene blue) applied sequentially to the same suspicious area in all 30 patients after VELscope examination; lesion-level counts per OPMD subgroup are given in Tables 1-3 but not aggregated overall.

site_selection_index_test: The clinician took at least five brush smears per lesion to be examined with the nylon brush; the head of the brush was placed tangentially to the oral lesion and rotated at least ten times.
specimen_collection: Between January 2009 and May 2012, the Cytobrush GT (Med-Scan Medical, Malmö, Sweden) was used for sampling; five brush smears were taken per lesion, the brush head placed tangentially and rotated at least ten times, then washed out in the preservation vial for liquid-based preparation.
technique: For both collectors, a liquid-based preparation method was used (SurePath™). Samples were shipped to an experienced pathologist, processed according to the SurePath™ protocol (cells deposited by gravitational force and transferred to glass slides), stained according to Papanicolaou (PAP), and evaluated using the German classification for extragenital cytology according to Böcking et al., which has four categories (negative, doubtful, suspicious, positive).
positivity_threshold: 'doubtful', 'suspicious' and 'positive' cytological results were overall considered as positive for malignancy in comparison to the final histological diagnoses; only 'negative' was reported as 'tumour cell negative'.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: doubtful/suspicious/positive cytology; negative: negative cytology
comments_index_test: This arm represents the earlier cohort (2009–2012) using the Cytobrush GT nylon brush, with five smears pooled per patient in one SurePath vial, in a consecutive and retrospective single-center study.

site_selection_index_test: The clinician took brush smears from conspicuous/clinically visible oral lesions; the head of the brush was placed tangentially to the oral lesion and rotated at least ten times.
specimen_collection: One brush smear per patient was obtained routinely using the rigid brush (Orcellex Brush), placed tangentially on the lesion and rotated at least ten times, then washed out in the preservation vial and processed by liquid-based cytology (SurePath).
technique: The Orcellex Brush was used once per lesion; the brush head was placed tangentially to the oral lesion and rotated at least ten times, then washed out thoroughly in the preservation vial. Specimens were shipped to a pathologist and processed according to the SurePath protocol, with cells deposited by gravitational force, transferred to glass slides, and stained by Papanicolaou (PAP). Evaluation followed the German classification for extragenital cytology (Böcking et al.).
positivity_threshold: Cytological results of 'doubtful', 'suspicious' and 'positive' were considered positive for malignancy ('tumour cell positive'); only 'negative' was considered negative ('tumour cell negative').
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: doubtful/suspicious/positive cytology; negative: negative cytology
comments_index_test: This was a retrospective comparison of two sequential cohorts (nylon brush 2009-2012, rigid brush 2012-2018) rather than a concurrent randomized comparison, which may introduce temporal confounding (e.g., differences in pathologist experience or referral patterns over time).

site_selection_index_test: Patients with clearly visible oral lesions, which showed apparent variation from the normal healthy mucosa, presenting to the Tokyo Dental College Hospital for new or follow-up appointments were screened for the study.
specimen_collection: Cell samples were collected using the Orcellex® Brush; after twisting the brush ten times, the head of the cell collector was transferred directly into an alcohol-based liquid in the BD SurePath™ Collection Vial and transported to the laboratory.
technique: Cytology was performed using BD SurePath™; cell samples were collected using the Orcellex® Brush; after twisting the brush ten times, the head of the cell collector was transferred into an alcohol-based liquid in the BD SurePath™ Collection Vial and transported to the laboratory; cells were stained with Papanicolaou stain according to the standard procedure; a detailed cytological assessment of cell quality and yield was performed using the modified 2014 Bethesda Cervical Cytology grading system.
positivity_threshold: To examine diagnostic ability via cytological and histological examinations, histology was classified as negative and positive (SCC) and cytology as negative (negative) and positive (doubtful, positive).
positivity_threshold_transformed: Positive: doubtful or positive cytology (malignant cells observed or suspected); Negative: no atypical cells observed
calibration_of_assessors: All participating experts had passed the board examination of the Japanese Society of Pathology for oral pathology and had been practicing for >7 years.
comments_index_test: Cytological diagnosis was independently assessed by at least two of five oral pathology diagnostic experts, with discrepancies settled by consensus; no explicit statement of blinding to histological results was found, which may affect risk-of-bias assessment.

index_test_reagent_name: 5% acetic acid and Lugol's iodine solution (1% iodine, 2% potassium iodide, 97% distilled water)
site_selection_index_test: Colposcopy was applied to the clinically suspected OPMD lesion in each patient; the lesion area was assessed under low/high magnification after saline wipe, and biopsy was subsequently taken from the most suspicious area identified.
technique: After wiping the mucosa with saline, the green filter was used to view vascular patterns at high magnification power (≥×30). Then, 5% acetic acid was applied to the lesion for about 60 seconds to assess for the aceto-whitening score at low magnification power (≤×20). Then, Lugol's solution was applied to the lesion to assess for the iodine intake score at low magnification power (≤×20). The RCI was then used to score the colposcopic signs (margin, color, vessels, iodine staining) for each case.
positivity_threshold: The cutoff value to segregate dysplastic lesions from nondysplastic lesions was 5 according to the RCI.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: RCI score ≥5
blinding_index_test_examiner: The colposcopic score for each participant was done by 2 assessors independently.
comments_index_test: This arm shares the same underlying colposcopic examination procedure (acetic acid + Lugol's iodine, same device) as the Swede scoring arm; only the scoring system (RCI vs Swede) and cutoff differ. Denominator of 25 lesions/patients was reduced by 2 cases 'missed for biopsy' (1 OLP, 1 OL), giving n=23 analyzed per histopathology in Table III.

index_test_reagent_name: 5% acetic acid and Lugol's iodine solution (1% iodine, 2% potassium iodide, 97% distilled water)
site_selection_index_test: NR
technique: After wiping the mucosa with saline, the green filter was used to view vascular patterns at high magnification power (≥×30). Then, 5% acetic acid was applied to the lesion for about 60 seconds to assess for the aceto-whitening score at low magnification power (≤×20). Then, Lugol's solution was applied to the lesion to assess for the iodine intake score at low magnification power (≤×20).
positivity_threshold: Swede score ≥8 indicates dysplastic lesion
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: Swede score ≥8
comments_index_test: This arm shares the same colposcopic examination procedure and raw colposcopic sign scores as the RCI arm; only the scoring system (Swede) and its cutoff (8) differ, meaning both arms are derived from overlapping/identical index-test data on the same patients.

site_selection_index_test: Whole oral cavity examined following standard clinical protocol, with suspect regions marked according to the Roed-Petersen topographical classification
technique: All patients were examined by the same experienced maxillofacial surgeon using the standard clinical protocol combined with the Roed-Petersen classification; the examination took place in a separate room with dimmed lights and safety goggles were worn; a suspect finding was based on visual inspection under white/incandescent light.
positivity_threshold: CA was positive when a suspect lesion was seen
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: suspect lesion seen on white-light examination
comments_index_test: All patients underwent both CA and AF examinations by the same surgeon in the same session; the two arms are not independent, which should be considered when interpreting comparative accuracy.

site_selection_index_test: Entire oral cavity examined using VELscope in a dimmed room; suspect regions identified by loss of fluorescence and marked per the Roed-Petersen protocol.
technique: The oral cavity was examined with VELscope and a Pentax reflex camera in a separate room with dimmed lights; safety goggles were worn by patient and examiner; a suspect finding was defined as loss of fluorescence.
positivity_threshold: A suspect finding in the VELscope assessment was defined as loss of fluorescence
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: loss of fluorescence
blinding_index_test_examiner: All patients were seen and examined by the same experienced maxillofacial surgeon.
comments_index_test: The decision to biopsy was based on either clinical or VELscope findings combined with clinician judgment, so the 39 biopsied patients are not exclusively VELscope-positive cases; sensitivity/specificity reported for combined CA+AF, not AF alone.

site_selection_index_test: Whole oral mucosa examined; suspicious areas identified on COE were re-examined with VELscope, and biopsy sites were selected based on fluorescence loss (or by clinical exam if VELscope negative)
technique: Conventional oral examination was done first, then the autofluorescence examination was followed using the Velscope (LED Medical Diagnostics Inc, Burnaby). Greenish fluorescence was considered normal/healthy mucosa; dark/brownish fluorescence was considered positive for dysplastic changes. Lesions were classified as Group 1 (fluorescence visualization loss, FVL) if they showed complete loss of autofluorescence, or Group 2 (fluorescence visualization retained, FVR) if autofluorescence patterns other than complete FVL were seen.
positivity_threshold: Lesions were rated as malignant or dysplastic only when there was a complete FVL; lesions showing autofluorescence patterns other than complete FVL were included in the FVR group
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: complete loss of autofluorescence (FVL/dark-brownish fluorescence)
comments_index_test: Biopsy site selection was guided by the index test itself (fluorescence loss dictated biopsy site when VELscope positive), which could introduce partial verification/incorporation bias since the reference standard site selection was influenced by the index test result.

site_selection_index_test: The conventional oral examination was done by trained field investigators for these subjects under white operatory light in Community Health Centers (CHC's) and primary health centers (PHC's)
technique: Conventional oral examination performed by trained field investigators under white operatory light, with a provisional clinical diagnosis noted based on visual inspection of the oral mucosa.
positivity_threshold: NR
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: clinically suspicious lesion on visual inspection
comments_index_test: White light examination had 12 cases (4.80%) with 'No Result' that were excluded from the 2x2 contingency table analysis (238 analyzed out of 250 total), which may affect comparability with the Velscope arm (n=250 analyzed).

site_selection_index_test: Smear taken from the oral lesion all over the lesion surface before biopsy
specimen_collection: One oral lesion smear was taken from each patient before biopsy using a cytobrush all over the lesion and stored at PreservCyt Thinprep
technique: Three cytologic slides were prepared for each lesion sample using the Cellspin I semi-automated cytocentrifuge system; slides were stained according to Papanicolaou and classified using an adaptation of Remmerbach et al., with results categorized as insufficient, negative for intraepithelial lesion and malignancy, low-grade lesion, high-grade lesion, suspicious for malignancy, or SCC.
positivity_threshold: High-risk cytologic results (high-grade lesion, suspicious for malignancy, or squamous cell carcinoma) were considered positive, whereas low-risk results (negative for intraepithelial lesion and malignancy or low-grade lesion) were considered negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: high-grade lesion, suspicious for malignancy, or SCC
comments_index_test: Two cytologists performed analyses independently, compared their results, and discussed discrepancies with a third cytologist, but no explicit statement on blinding to histopathology results was provided.

site_selection_index_test: One oral lesion smear was taken from each patient using a cytobrush all over the lesion before biopsy; DNA-ICM performed on the same slide.
specimen_collection: Cytobrush smear from the oral lesion, stored in PreservCyt Thinprep, with DNA-ICM performed on the same slide as cytology after Feulgen-Schiff staining.
technique: Slides uncovered in xylene and stained by the Feulgen-Schiff method (Merck); DNA ploidy analyses performed using a semi-automated DNA cytometer MotiCyte DNA Cytology Work Station (Motic), with a computer attached to a Motic BA410 microscope and Moticam Pro 285A camera. Nuclear content analysis performed according to the 4th ESACP Consensus. Individual nuclei with definable boundaries were selected. At least 35 normal oral epithelial cell nuclei were selected for calibration reference; integrated optical density values converted to reference values of 2c; coefficient of variation <5% adopted for quality assurance. After calibration, a minimum of 200 nuclei per slide were randomly selected, with cells of suspicious nuclear morphology arbitrarily included. Data analyzed using MotiCyte software version 2, classifying results as euploid or aneuploid.
positivity_threshold: The sample was considered aneuploid if a stemline DNA index was <0.90 and >1.10 or <1.80 and >2.20 or <3.60 and >4.40 or if there were cells with exceeding 9c content.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: aneuploid (DNA index outside 0.90-1.10, 1.80-2.20, 3.60-4.40 ranges, or cells >9c)
calibration_of_assessors: For calibration reference, at least 35 nuclei of normal oral epithelial cells were selected; for quality assurance, a coefficient of variation of reference cells of <5% was adopted.
comments_index_test: DNA-ICM was performed on the same slide/sample as cytology; the number of patients analyzed for DNA-ICM (83) differs from the total cohort (98) due to inadequate samples (16 total inadequate for cytology and/or DNA ploidy per Figure 2).

site_selection_index_test: Biopsy site decided clinically based on the consultant's visual examination of the lesion (used for non-stained lesions and as the reference for clinical diagnosis)
technique: All patients were registered and examined by the consultant Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeon, who grouped lesions as benign, premalignant, or malignant based on clinical appearance; a biopsy was then planned under local anesthesia.
positivity_threshold: Clinical diagnosis categorized as premalignant or malignant (positive) versus benign (negative)
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: premalignant or malignant clinical impression
comments_index_test: Clinical examination was performed by a single consultant Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeon for all cases, which may limit inter-observer variability but also limits generalizability; the paper notes clinical assessment is subjective and may differ between clinicians.

site_selection_index_test: Biopsy was taken from the stained sites; in non-stained lesions, the site of the biopsy was decided clinically.
specimen_collection: Biopsy specimens were taken from the stained (or clinically decided) sites and sent to the Department of Histopathology.
technique: Patients rinsed with water, then given 1% acetic acid mouthwash for 20 seconds; 1% Toluidine blue was then applied to the lesion with a cotton swab, followed by acetic acid mouthwash to remove excess stain; staining was recorded as positive or negative irrespective of intensity.
positivity_threshold: The staining is recorded as positive or negative irrespective of the intensity of the stain.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: any stain uptake (irrespective of intensity)
comments_index_test: Staining and biopsy site selection were performed by the same consultant Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeon who also did clinical assessment, which could introduce assessment overlap/bias between the two index test arms (clinical exam vs toluidine blue).

site_selection_index_test: Biopsy site selected based on clinical suspicion (inspection and palpation) of the pre-malignant or malignant lesion, taken as a wedge including the margins of the lesion
specimen_collection: Wedge biopsy and histopathological analysis under local anesthesia were done by a single surgeon, from the edge of the lesion without staining in Group A
technique: Clinical examination was performed by a single expert otorhinolaryngologist using inspection and palpation to assess location, size, extent of local infiltration, oral hygiene, and cervical lymph node status; biopsy was then taken from the area of most clinical suspicion without any staining
positivity_threshold: Clinical suspicion (by inspection and palpation) of a pre-malignant or malignant lesion
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: clinical suspicion of premalignant/malignant lesion on inspection and palpation
blinding_index_test_assessors: The pathologists examining the biopsy specimens were not informed regarding the staining information of the samples
comments_index_test: This arm represents the conventional biopsy method based solely on clinical suspicion (no staining), serving as the comparator to Toluidine Blue-guided biopsy in Group B; a single expert clinician performed all examinations to reduce bias

index_test_arm_label: Vital Staining (1% Toluidine Blue) - Group B
site_selection_index_test: In Group B, biopsy was done from the area stained maximum with Toluidine Blue, as determined by the dye uptake pattern observed under proper light and exposure.
specimen_collection: Wedge biopsy and histopathological analysis under local anesthesia were done by a single surgeon, from the edge of the lesion after staining with Toluidine Blue.
technique: 1% Toluidine Blue solution was prepared from 1 gm Toluidine Blue dye powder, 10 ml 1% Acetic Acid, 4.19 ml Absolute Alcohol, and 86 ml Distilled Water. The mouth was first rinsed with water to remove debris, then a 1% Acetic Acid rinse was given for 20 s to remove saliva, and the area was dried with gauze. The dye was then applied over the oral lesion with a cotton swab, very gently, for 1 min, covering approximately 2 cm margin all around the lesion. A 1% Acetic Acid rinse was given thereafter for 1 min and the dye uptake pattern was observed under proper light and exposure. Gentle swabbing with 1% Acetic Acid was done to remove excess stain.
positivity_threshold: A stain was considered positive for malignancy if the lesion diffusely or partly stained dark blue (royal or navy blue), or had stippled appearance. A negative stain means no absorption of the dye. All equivocal lesions were considered positively stained unless proved otherwise.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark blue/stippled stain uptake; negative: no dye absorption
blinding_index_test_assessors: The pathologists examining the biopsy specimens were not informed regarding the staining information of the samples.
comments_index_test: NR

site_selection_index_test: Patients with symptoms and signs suggestive of oral premalignant lesions and suspected oral malignancy identified on head and neck examination were subjected to toluidine blue staining of the identified lesions
technique: Rinse mouth with water for 20s to remove debris; apply 1% acetic acid for 20s to remove ropey saliva; apply 1% toluidine blue oral rinse for 20s; rinse again with 1% acetic acid to remove mechanically retained stain; finally rinse with water.
positivity_threshold: Lesions that exhibited dark blue staining were deemed positive for premalignant or malignant tissue, while those with light staining or no color were considered negative
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark blue stain uptake; negative: light staining or no stain
blinding_index_test_assessors: The pathologists who examined the biopsies were not informed about the clinical or staining evaluations of the samples, indicating the reference standard assessors were blinded to the index test results; blinding of index test assessors to reference standard is not explicitly stated.
comments_index_test: The staining protocol described (water rinse, acetic acid, toluidine blue, acetic acid, water rinse) follows the Mashberg technique cited as reference [16]; concentration reported inconsistently as 1% in text but bottle image shows 0.1% solution labeled 'TOLUIDINE BLUE 0.1% SOLUTION', suggesting a possible discrepancy in reported concentration.

site_selection_index_test: Biopsy site selected based on clinical appearance and dye retention (toluidine blue uptake); acetic acid was applied to the entire clinically identified lesion
technique: Five percent acetic acid was applied to the lesion with a sterile disposable cotton applicator for 60 seconds. A photograph of the lesion was taken again following this. The lesion was observed for any color changes following the application of acetic acid.
positivity_threshold: The results of the acetic acid application were considered positive if the lesion appears opaque white (acetowhite) and a negative if the lesion does not show any color change.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: acetowhite (opaque white) change
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded; a single examiner performed all observations and clinical examination
comments_index_test: Acetic acid was applied first, followed by toluidine blue on the same lesion in the same patient, so both tests were performed on the same lesion sequentially, which could introduce order effects; a single examiner performed all assessments, and blinding to reference standard was not explicitly reported.

site_selection_index_test: The site of the biopsy was selected based on the clinical appearance and dye retention.
specimen_collection: A biopsy was obtained from the lesion and subjected to histopathological examination.
technique: After the application of acetic acid, 1% toluidine blue was applied to the lesion with a sterile disposable cotton applicator for 60 seconds and decolorized with acetic acid. A photograph of the lesion was taken following this procedure.
positivity_threshold: The lesion was considered toluidine blue positive if it retained blue color after the staining. Lesions with no uptake or questionable uptake constituted the negative toluidine blue category of lesions.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: retained blue stain (questionable/no uptake = negative)
blinding_index_test_examiner: The subjectivity in visual examination was not investigated as a single examiner performed all the observations.
comments_index_test: Toluidine blue was applied after acetic acid on the same lesions in all 31 patients (sequential application, not independent arms); biopsy site was influenced by both acetic acid appearance and toluidine blue dye retention, which could introduce incorporation bias/interdependence between the two index tests.

index_test_arm_label: Vital Staining (2% Toluidine Blue Electrospun Fiber Patch)
index_test_reagent_name: 2% w/v toluidine blue (electrospun fiber patch with 10% w/v PVP)
site_selection_index_test: All lesions suspected as OPMDs or non-healing ulcers >2 weeks without identifiable cause were identified during oral examination and stained with the patch; lesions >2cm covered with multiple patches placed adjacent to each other
technique: A cotton tip was used to apply 1% acetic acid to the lesion for 20s to eliminate residue layers; then a 2x2cm electrospun fiber patch containing 2% TB was applied to the lesion for 20s; finally, mechanically retained stain was removed by applying 1% acetic acid with a cotton tip for 20s; one oral medicine dentist measured color and intensity of staining
positivity_threshold: Dark royal blue staining was considered positive; pale or no staining was considered negative
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark blue stain; negative: pale/no stain
blinding_index_test_assessors: The oral pathologist performing histopathological examination was blinded to the tissue staining results, but it is not explicitly stated whether the dentist applying/reading the TB staining was blinded to histopathology results (which had not yet occurred).
comments_index_test: Only one index test arm was used in this study (TB-containing electrospun fiber patch, 2% w/v TB); no comparison to standard TB staining protocols was performed, a noted limitation by the authors.

index_test_reagent_name: hBD-2 and hBD-3 antibody pairs (ELISA) used to quantify the hBD-3/hBD-2 ratio
index_test_commercial_name: Defensin 2, beta (Human) - ELISA Kit and Defensin 3, beta (Human) - ELISA Kit (Phoenix Pharmaceuticals)
site_selection_index_test: The clinician applied the cytobrush onto the mucosal surface of the suspicious lesion, then performed the same procedure on the contralateral normal side of the oral cavity, before biopsy.
specimen_collection: Cytobrush samples were collected from the lesion and contralateral normal sites using the Rovers Orcellex Brush; the brush was turned 10 times with pressure to collect cells, then placed into a collection tube with 2 mL PBS and stored on ice/-80°C until ELISA processing.
technique: Paired cytobrush samples were thawed, cells dislodged and lysed in RIPA buffer, centrifuged, and the supernatant used for a sandwich ELISA with hBD-2 and hBD-3 antibody pairs (Peprotech for discovery/internal validation; Phoenix Pharmaceuticals kits for external validation). BDI was calculated as [OD_hBD-3/OD_hBD-2]_Lesion / [OD_hBD-3/OD_hBD-2]_Normal.
positivity_threshold: BDI cutoff value of 1.25; a value at or above 1.25 indicates cancer
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: BDI ≥ 1.25
calibration_of_assessors: To avoid inter-operator variability, the same clinician collected paired cytobrush samples from the lesion and contralateral sites of each subject in the discovery study; one laboratory operator generated BDI values.
blinding_index_test_assessors: The samples were intentionally blinded so that pathologist-determined diagnoses were revealed only after BDI scores were obtained for all patients.
comments_index_test: This row aggregates the ELISA-based BDI arm across the discovery phase (n=40) and the three validation cohorts (internal n=21, external 1 n=19, external 2 n=12; total validation n=52), giving a combined total of 92 subjects as reported in Table 1 and Table S3.

site_selection_index_test: Clinically suspicious/doubtful oral lesions identified on examination under artificial illumination were selected for staining
technique: After recording clinical features and photograph of clinically suspicious lesions, the lesion areas were pretreated with 1% acetic acid using a cotton bud for 20 seconds, repeated once, then rinsed with water. Toluidine blue was then applied with a cotton bud for 10 to 20 seconds. The lesion was decolorized with 2% acetic acid using a cotton bud for 20-30 seconds and a photograph was taken.
positivity_threshold: Dark blue was considered as positive for lesions suspicious of malignancy, light blue retention was considered as positive for premalignant lesions unless proved otherwise by biopsy, and lesion without retention was considered negative
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: any stain retention (dark blue or light blue); negative: no stain retention
comments_index_test: Single-arm study; all 100 patients underwent toluidine blue staining, and the same patients underwent incisional biopsy as reference standard; the 2x2 table (Table 6) reports dye retention (+/-) vs histological diagnosis (dysplastic+malignant vs benign) at the patient level.

site_selection_index_test: The main site of morphologically altered mucosa was selected and photographed prior to TB application
technique: 1%TB is applied in 4 steps; first, rinsing of oral cavity with water for 20 s to remove debris, then application or rinse with 1% acetic acid for 20 s, after that application or rinse with TB solution (1% W/W) for 20 s and finally application or rinse with 1% acetic acid for 20 s to eliminate mechanically retained stains.
positivity_threshold: A royal blue or a navy blue stain was considered as a positive result even if either the entire lesion or a portion of the lesion is stained or stippled. A light blue staining is considered doubtful. If there is no colour absorbed by the lesion, it was taken as a negative stain.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: royal/navy blue stain retention
calibration_of_assessors: Dental surgeons in the selected institutions were trained by the expert in the field of Oral Medicine at their institutions. Live demonstrations of TB application were carried out to familiarise the procedure during the training programme.
comments_index_test: In TB-positive cases, biopsy was taken from the TB-positive region, while in TB-negative cases biopsy was taken from the clinical site, which could introduce differential verification/workup bias affecting accuracy estimates.

site_selection_index_test: An oral medicine specialist recorded clinical findings, took pictures of the lesions, and picked the areas to be examined.
specimen_collection: Incisional biopsy performed at the blue-stained area following toluidine blue application.
technique: A cotton bud soaked in 1% acetic acid was used to clean the lesion prior to the application of toluidine blue with a different cotton tip for 30 s. Subsequently, a third cotton bud soaked with 1% acetic acid was used to remove any excess toluidine blue on the lesion. The patient then rinsed out their mouth.
positivity_threshold: A positive lesion was the one which color changed to blue, while a negative lesion was with no change.
positivity_threshold_transformed: Positive: blue stain retained
comments_index_test: Note discrepancy: 33 patients were randomized to receive toluidine blue, but the results table (Table 2) reports 67 specimens from 54 patients for this arm; it is unclear if this includes multiple lesions per patient or a different patient count than initially randomized.

site_selection_index_test: An oral medicine specialist recorded clinical findings, took pictures of the lesions, and picked the areas to be examined.
specimen_collection: An incisional biopsy was performed at the area that had turned opaque white.
technique: A gauze soaked with vinegar was applied to a clean and dry lesion for one minute; the researcher noted the changes and took a picture of the lesion. A positive finding was designated when a lesion changed to opaque white; when a lesion did not change or changed to transparent white, a negative finding was indicated.
positivity_threshold: A positive finding was designated when a lesion changed to opaque white. When a lesion did not change or changed to transparent white, a negative finding was indicated.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: opaque white staining
comments_index_test: Methods describe a 'second group of 30 patients' receiving only vinegar, but the diagnostic accuracy analysis in Table 3 (83 specimens from 57 patients) appears to pool this vinegar-only subgroup with the combined TB+vinegar subgroup (24 patients), since vinegar was applied to both groups; this should be considered when interpreting the denominators for this arm.
